name: Aït Benhaddou
hero_subtitle: UNESCO mud-brick village — the silhouette everyone knows from film and postcards.

overview.title: The Classic Ksar on the Old Caravan Road
overview.p1: Aït Benhaddou is the ksar that defined the postcard of southern Morocco for many travellers: a cluster of earthen buildings climbing a hillside above a seasonal river, about thirty minutes from Ouarzazate. It is a living village as well as a UNESCO site, which means you share the lanes with residents, guides and tour groups.
overview.p2: Cross the riverbed (or the bridge when the water is up), climb toward the granary at the top, and give yourself time on the way down. The view back over the valley is the reason the climb is worth the heat.
overview.p3: Early morning is the difference between a calm visit and a crowded one. Midday on the open mud slopes is harsh from late spring onward.

q2.question: Is there an entry fee?
q2.answer: A community fee is usual at the entrance — small notes help.

q3.question: Can I stay overnight?
q3.answer: A few simple guesthouses exist; most visitors day-trip from Ouarzazate.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Aït Benhaddou?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and safe paths on fragile mud brick.

q5.question: Is Aït Benhaddou suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with supervision on steps, rooftops and uneven ground.

food.title: Simple meals near the ksar
food.p1: Cafés and tagine spots sit on the modern side of the river. Inside the ksar, expect little beyond tea if anything.
food.p2: Eat where other travellers and locals are sitting — turnover matters in the heat.
food.li1: Tagine with a view on the new side
food.li4: Avoid undercooked salads if your stomach is sensitive
food.li5: Lunch back in town if you prefer more choice

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Aït Benhaddou

1.title: Arrive early
1.desc: Coach groups peak mid-morning to early afternoon. Before 9–10 am the lanes are quieter and the mud is cooler underfoot.

2.title: River crossing
2.desc: In dry months you walk the riverbed; after rain use the bridge. Shoes you do not mind getting dusty are essential.

3.title: Guides
3.desc: Official guides wait at the entrance. Useful for history; not required if you only want the climb and the view. Agree the price before you start.
